cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 and T7 answer the Stoic directly: indifference is not the goal, thought-change is too passive.
cells.limitation: T2, T5, T8 append Taleb's angle without engaging; T9 restates T6 instead of answering T7.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 adds that feeling behind reflects lacking a committed project.
cells.limitation: No mid-debate distinction later used; T6 and T9 repeat T3's indifference claim.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4/T7 versus T6: inner reframing against committed action.
cells.limitation: User's ambivalence about wanting these milestones, and loneliness or belonging, never examined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 tries to fold Sartre's action into robust, status-free commitments.
cells.limitation: T9 'Exactly' closes in agreement without addressing T7's passivity objection.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names the open dispute: ignore milestones or build a life making them irrelevant.
cells.limitation: Ending no sharper than T1; D asserts the user lives passively rather than clarifying.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 grants the Stoic's point on perspective before disagreeing.
cells.limitation: T2 treats the user as herd-following though user doubts wanting milestones; T7 flattens Stoicism to passivity.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T7 objects that changing thoughts cannot escape the anxiety of freedom.
cells.limitation: T9 restates indifference rather than answering T7; no objection says what breaks if false.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 bad faith and T6 thoughts-shape-happiness broadly track their sources.
cells.limitation: T3 opinion/perspective line is a known misattribution (suspected); T8 antifragile comes from a later Taleb book.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section D separates the main insight from what remains disputed.
cells.limitation: T1, T7 and section D state the user's motive and passivity as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 concedes 'The Stoic is right about perspective'.
cells.limitation: No claim revised; Stoic ignores T7's objection; Taleb's 'True' and 'I agree' concede nothing specific.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames whether feeling behind signals neglected needs or mere comparison.
cells.limitation: Debate drops the user's uncertainty about wanting the milestones at all.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T5 notes friends may have different risk tolerances and resources.
cells.limitation: Only the two milestones are used; generic advice could fit anyone.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on belonging versus autonomy.
cells.limitation: Speakers impose their own schools' goods (T9 character) instead of the user's priorities.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 mentions resources and risk tolerance.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts the user is suffering; no timing, relationship or money stakes considered.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E offers conditional branches on priorities.
cells.limitation: No question asks whether the user wants partnership or a home; T3 question is rhetorical.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E contrasts craving security with desiring self-definition.
cells.limitation: T1 and T7 assert why the user feels behind; no alternative motives offered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 asks why friends get the power to define success.
cells.limitation: Assumption that 'behind' implies one timeline never unpacked; rhetorical rather than examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E sets social belonging and stability against autonomy.
cells.limitation: Value conflict appears only in the synthesis, not developed in the turns.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: Section A names social comparison pressure.
cells.limitation: T1 labels the feeling bad faith; fear of being left out or alone never named.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E lets the user pick which priority applies.
cells.limitation: Turns deliver verdicts (T6, T9 'will vanish') rather than distinctions to accept or refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section D frames ignoring milestones versus building a life rendering them irrelevant.
cells.limitation: No concrete options defined, such as pursuing, postponing or declining either milestone.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T5 points to the payoff of milestones against personal resources.
cells.limitation: No cost of opting out, such as drifting from friends, is ever named.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if belonging matters most, investigate whether milestones offer security.
cells.limitation: Conditions are abstract priorities, not anything the user could observe or count.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D notes the Stoic-Existentialist dispute remains open.
cells.limitation: Key unknown, whether the user wants these things, never separated as consequential.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: invest in one area you control and watch comparison diminish.
cells.limitation: Step is vague and not derived from the debate's analysis.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 explains anti-fragile as things improving life regardless of friends.
cells.limitation: T1 bad faith and T7 anxiety of freedom go unexplained for a lay reader.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 names 'The Stoic' explicitly before disagreeing.
cells.limitation: T7 'That is too passive' and T9 'Exactly' leave targets implicit.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: Strict rotation and near-identical turn lengths make pacing monotonous.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Three schools hold distinct positions: authenticity, robustness, indifference.
cells.limitation: All three share one lecturing second-person register; no explicit position change.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns are short and avoid long recaps.
cells.limitation: T6 and T9 repeat T3's indifference point without adding anything.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T7 versus T6 pits action against inner reframing.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; nothing the user could lose or gain is made vivid.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T4 partially agrees with the Stoic before turning.
cells.limitation: No speaker changes position at any point.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T5 'playing a game designed by people' gives Taleb some edge.
cells.limitation: Voices are generic summaries of schools; Taleb lacks his characteristic bite.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5's game designed by others with different risk tolerances.
cells.limitation: No concrete example or analogy grounded in the user's situation.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T7's sharp 'That is too passive' briefly lifts intensity.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm throughout; T9 ends flat with a promise the feeling will vanish.

strengths: Section A frames a real tension: feeling behind as signal versus social comparison.
T4 and T7 give the Existentialist genuine pushback against the Stoic's inner-reframing view.
Section E offers conditional branches on belonging versus autonomy plus a small next step.
weaknesses: T1, T7 and section D assert the user's motive and passivity as fact, never asking.
The debate ignores the user's stated doubt about wanting marriage or a home; no questions posed.
Stoic T9 ignores T7's objection; no speaker revises, so the ending is forced agreement.

symptoms.observed: Speakers declare why the user feels behind instead of offering alternative motives.
symptoms.evidence: If you feel behind, it is because you have not yet committed

symptoms.observed: No question asks whether the user wants these milestones; T2 assumes herd-following.
symptoms.evidence: Following the herd into marriage or home ownership just because

symptoms.observed: Stoic answers T7's passivity objection with agreement-word and restatement, no revision.
symptoms.evidence: Exactly. Whether you marry or buy a home is a matter

symptoms.observed: Stoic opening line is a suspected misattribution; antifragile belongs to a later book.
symptoms.evidence: Everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact.

symptoms.observed: No cost of opting out of milestones is named; only costs of conforming.
symptoms.evidence: Do not commit to a house or a marriage to signal

findings.description: The opinion/perspective line is widely attributed to Marcus Aurelius but does not appear to be in Meditations.
Anti-fragility is the concept of Taleb's Antifragile (2012), not The Black Swan cited as basis.
The user's motive and passivity are stated as fact without evidence from the situation.

rubric_fit_notes: Labelled decision (self_reflection) though the user names no concrete choice; read criterion 5 against the implicit choice of whether to pursue or let go of these milestones. Turn 3 attribution judgment rests on memory only.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision with a self-reflective core, so criterion 5 was scored on the implicit pursue-or-release choice and criterion 4 weighed heavily.
